newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up, demand increases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up, demand increases.

text.p: Spring wheat bids were higher on Thursday as MGE futures rose and spot demand increased, several U.S. cash grain merchants said.
"It seems like the basis firmed up a little bit," a Minnesota dealer said. "People are short and needing to buy some wheat before the lakes close up."
He said the Great Lakes shipping channels normally close in mid- to late December but the exact date depends on weather conditions. An early freeze would close the channels sooner.
Farmer selling remained slow in most areas as farmers held out for higher prices.
Many farmers opted to put new crop supplies under USDA loan for an average price of $2.25 to $2.50 per bushel.

If prices go up by the time the loans are due, farmers would repay the money and sell the wheat at a profit, dealers explained. If prices fall, farmers can default on the loan and give up the grain to the Commodity Credit Corp.
"They're willing to do just about anything to keep that grain out of market," a Montana dealer said.
